messages.reasoning_content:
The data is:
- 180 features
- 8000 visitors
- 14283 visitor_feature records
- 16200 feature_daily_metrics rows (90 days × 180 features = 16200, so each feature has 90 days of metrics)
- 8000 CLV insights (one per visitor)
- 180 adoption analytics
- 1000 accounts

The date range is 2025-07-16 to 2025-10-13 (90 days).

The task: quantify contribution of different features to CLV, identify "hidden value features" - low usage frequency (monthly active visitors < 200) but significant positive impact on customer value.

Approach:
1. Define CLV proxy from customer_lifecycle_insights - there's `comprehensive_customer_value`, `user_value_score`, `predicted_clv_tier`, `predicted_ltv_tier`, `rfm_composite_score`, etc. Let me examine those.
2. Compute feature usage: monthly active visitors per feature. Since we have 90 days (about 3 months), we could compute active visitors by month or just use overall active visitors. The definition "monthly active visitors < 200" - we can compute monthly active visitors from feature_daily_metrics (unique visitors per month) or from visitor_feature. Actually, feature_daily_metrics has count_visitors per day per feature; summing distinct visitors per month requires deduplication. Let me think about what's the cleanest way.

Let me check the columns in the CLV insights table more carefully and understand the value metrics. Also let me look at visitor_feature to understand the linkage.

The core analysis idea:
- For each feature, identify the set of visitors who used it (from visitor_feature table).
- Compute average CLV (comprehensive_customer_value) of users who used the feature vs. users who did not use it. The difference is the "value contribution" of the feature.
- Filter for features with low usage (monthly active visitors < 200) but significant positive impact.

Let me examine the CLV table first.

function.name: dacomp_answer
function.description: Submit the final Markdown report. Reference figures by relative workspace paths. Stop after submission.

function.name: dacomp_file
function.description: Read or write task workspace files; read result archives in chunks. Workspace paths are relative. Results can be read as results/S1.rows.jsonl.

function.name: dacomp_list_db
function.description: List database tables and schema via recorded metadata SQL.

function.name: dacomp_python
function.description: Run analysis Python for visualization or SQL-unsupported statistics. Explain why outside SQL. Globals: db.query(sql, parameters=[]), db.executemany(sql, parameter_sets), db.executescript(sql), db.rows(result), db.frame(result). Complete archives at /results/<S>.rows.jsonl; save figures in /work using relative paths. Available numpy, pandas, scipy, matplotlib, seaborn. Raw SQLite/network/subprocess access unavailable.

function.name: dacomp_query_db
function.description: Execute SQLite SQL on the supplied read-only database. All statements, bound parameters and full row arrays are archived. Multiple statements and parameter batches are recorded individually. Result preview is limited; complete results are available to Python via db.rows/db.frame.
